newsitem.title: GERMANY: German govt official to run Deutsche Bahn.
newsitem.headline: German govt official to run Deutsche Bahn.

text.p: German government officials confirmed on Monday that a senior aide to Chancellor Helmut Kohl would be appointed to run the national railway Deutsche Bahn AG.

The Transport Ministry confirmed press reports which said Johannes Ludewig, state secretary in the Economics Ministry, would be appointed to head the railway at a meeting of the supervisory board later on Monday.
Current Deutsche Bahn chairman Heinz Duerr would take a seat on the supervisory board, officials said.
The final decision about Duerr's successor would be taken by the supervisory board on February 26.

Deutsche Bahn spokeswoman Anfried Baier-Fuchs declined to comment, but she told Reuters the supervisory board presidium might issue a news release after a meeting on Monday night. The board was expected to meet to discuss a successor to Duerr.
"The presidium will meet tonight and may have news after the meeting," Baier-Fuchs said.
Ludewig, a close ally of Chancellor Helmut Kohl, has served in government since 1975, in the Economics Ministry and in the Chancellory.
From 1991 to 1994 Ludewig served as director of economic and financial policy in the Chancellory and coordinator for rebuilding east Germany following German unification in 1990.
The opposition Social Democrats said naming Ludewig to head Deutsche Bahn would hinder the railway's conversion from a state bureaucracy to an independent corporation.

Norbert Hansen, deputy chairman of the German Railway Workers Union (GdE), said he had nothing against Ludewig's appointment, but that the union's approval would depend on how Ludewig approaches the issue of cutting jobs.
The union is represented on the supervisory board.
